subject: Life Skills
title: Anchoring and Price Perception
description: A 60-second lesson on Anchoring and Price Perception.

hook.text: A jacket on sale from $200 to $100 feels like a steal. The same jacket at $100 full price feels expensive. Same jacket.

buildup.text: Anchoring means the first number you see sets your mental reference point. Everything after is judged relative to it.

discovery.text: Retailers exploit this ruthlessly. The original price exists solely to make the discount look irresistible.

twist.text: Even knowing about anchoring does not eliminate it. Your brain still feels the pull. Awareness only adds a speed bump.

climax.text: Before buying on sale, ask: would I buy this at the sale price if there was no original price shown? If no, walk away.

punchline.text: Ignore the anchor. Judge the price on its own.

quiz.question: How does anchoring affect purchase decisions?
options: It makes you buy the cheapest option available
The first price you see sets a reference that distorts your price judgment
It only works on large purchases like houses or cars
